Context (the bet)

Santander runs a group-wide strategy — ONE Transformation, "a digital bank with branches" — measured on customer growth, NPS, and cost-to-serve. Openbank is its 100%-digital arm. In late 2024 it entered the US: no branches, a market ruled by Chase/BofA/Wells, competing on experience and rate. The job was to make opening and trusting a brand-new digital bank effortless enough to win deposits at national scale.

The problem I worked on

[FILL IN — frame as a design problem, not a business one. Examples to pick from:]

  • Onboarding: getting a stranger from "never heard of Openbank" to a funded FDIC-insured account in under four minutes, with trust intact.
  • Verizon handoff: one journey spanning two brands — verizon.com/MyVerizon → Openbank account opening → a rewards mechanic tied to daily balance — without dropping users at the seam.
  • Debit card / CX: [your Jan-2024 story — CX absent from review; card missing digital-bank branding].
  • New products: bringing CDs / checking / payments onto a consistent system as the shelf expanded.

Outcomes

  • Deposits: $0 → $2B (Feb '25) → $6B (Oct '25) → ~$11.4B (Jun '26).
  • Customers: 0 → 100k in six months → ~235k.
  • The hook: grew deposits as the headline APY fell 5.00% → 3.80% — not rate-chasing.
  • Verizon: >$1.3B deposits via the partnership since Apr '25.
  • NPS: Santander US rose 6th → 3rd (2024→2025), audited, vs. Chase/BofA/Wells/Capital One.
  • Your private proof: [FILL IN — onboarding conversion / time-to-open / internal CSAT / reprint $ saved]

Honest framing (keeps it credible)

Design shares credit with rate, brand, and Verizon distribution. Claim contribution, attach to Santander's own words — it credits the US "customer experience through improvements in usability, transparency, speed and reliability" — and lead with the metric you can defend (NPS, onboarding). Don't claim you drove deposits or profit alone. (Complaints rose bank-wide on a bigger base — leave it out unless asked.)

What this shows about me
